reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

Freedom isn't free. Our nation’s freedom and democracy endure because of the brave men and women who have answered the call to serve. 

West Virginia has a strong history of defending our country, and today we honor that legacy. To all the Veterans and their families across West Virginia and our great nation, thank you for your service and sacrifice.

Happy 251st Birthday to the United States Marine Corps!

For more than two and a half centuries, the brave men and women of the Marine Corps have answered our nation’s call with unwavering courage and sacrifice. From defending our freedoms abroad to protecting the American people here at home, Marines have proudly upheld the values that make our nation great.

Today, we honor their extraordinary legacy and thank every Marine who has worn the uniform. Semper Fi! 🇺🇸

This past August, students from this chapter had 109 individual exhibits entered into the WV State Fair, and brought home https://t.co/EPIgnpdLcj

Reminder: Applications for a Military Academy Nomination are due to my office by October 30 at 6:00 p.m.! Our nation’s prestigious service academies are a wonderful opportunity to receive a world-class education and prepare for a future career in the armed services.

I would encourage all interested students to visit my website, where more information can be found under the “Services” tab.

Today, we celebrate the U.S. Navy's 251st Birthday! I am incredibly grateful to all the sailors and Navy veterans in my district and across the nation who answered the call of duty. Your unwavering service does not go unrecognized, and I thank you for all that you do! https://t.co/BImIgyyi5d

It was wonderful to be at Marshall University‘s Bill Noe Flight School celebrating their partnership with BETA Technologies and seeing their new all-electric planes take an inaugural flight. 

Marshall continues to reach new heights and prepare their students by anticipating the demands of tomorrow’s workforce today. I commend Marshall University for its dedication to investing in both its students and in our state’s future. This initiative will strengthen critical cargo and medical transport across West Virginia, opening new doors for innovation and economic development right here in Almost Heaven.

Three years ago today, the world witnessed unimaginable evil as Hamas terrorists brutally attacked Israel, murdering more than 1,200 innocent people and taking hundreds of people hostage.

Three years later, Jewish communities continue to face a disturbing rise in antisemitism and hatred. There is no place for antisemitism in America or anywhere in the world, and we must never remain silent in the face of it.

Today, we mourn the innocent lives stolen on October 7th, stand with the victims and their families, and reaffirm our unwavering support for the Jewish people.

posts.text: It was great to tour Elana Health and be joined by WV Durable Medical Equipment Providers to discuss their work improving health outcomes, increasing patient independence, and reducing overall healthcare costs. West Virginia is healthier and stronger thanks to their dedicated work! Thank you for having me!

I had the opportunity to meet with Roger Calhoun, the state director and president of AARP West Virginia. AARP is doing great work supporting its members and enhancing their quality of life. Through a wide range of programs and services, AARP continues to be a valuable resource for older Americans and their families. I appreciate their commitment to serving our communities and helping West Virginians live healthy, fulfilling lives!

It was wonderful to sit down with KVC West Virginia to hear about the incredible work they do supporting families, children in need, and helping our state’s foster children find safe and loving homes. 

Each year, KVC helps over 3,000 individuals with their wraparound services, including foster care, adoption, therapy, and foster parent training. They are truly a blessing to our state!

On #NationalManufacturingDay, we celebrate the hardworking West Virginians who build and power America. With a strong industrial base and a skilled workforce, West Virginia is proudly manufacturing America’s future. 🇺🇸 https://t.co/b215n6i3h9

West Virginia’s natural beauty is second to none! I’m happy to have supported this project to protect an additional 276 acres along the New River Gorge National Park and Preserve. You can read more about this announcement below!

https://t.co/o8qntuykCO

Recently, I had the opportunity to meet with Kazakhstan’s First Deputy Foreign Minister Yerzhan Ashikbayev to discuss the progress being made toward removing Jackson-Vanik restrictions. I am grateful for the conversation and look forward to continuing our work together. Always a pleasure to connect with our friends in Kazakhstan!

Today is National Falls Prevention Awareness Day, a day to raise awareness about the serious risks falls pose to older Americans and the steps we can take to prevent them.

This Congress, I introduced the SAFE Act to help ensure seniors have access to fall risk assessments as part of their Medicare Annual Wellness Visit. We must continue raising awareness and making sure our seniors have the tools they need to stay safe and independent!

It was wonderful to visit Bluefield State University and speak with members of the Student Government Association as well as instructors for the Mining Engineering Program. Bluefield State University is continuing to expand their offerings and is preparing our next generation well for their bright futures ahead!

It was great to visit with the staff of WVU Medicine Princeton Community Hospital. 

Just last month, the Princeton Community Hospital Association was awarded a $750,000 grant through the Rural Residency Planning and Development Program to expand and improve access to health care in rural communities. In December, I introduced the legislation to authorize this program, and I am delighted to see it benefiting our rural areas of southern West Virginia.

With the new school year well underway, it is a great time for our high school students here in West Virginia to start planning the next steps in their education! Our nation’s prestigious service academies are a wonderful opportunity to receive a world-class education and prepare for a future career in the armed services.

I would encourage all interested students to look over the flyer below and visit my website, where more information can be found under the “Services” tab. Applications for a Military Academy Nomination are due to my office by October 30 at 6:00 p.m.

239 years ago, our Founding Fathers came together and signed the cornerstone of our nation, the Constitution. This document has protected our God-given freedoms and liberties for over two centuries and has guided our nation for generations. Today we honor and remember the principles that make America so special.
What incredible news! Praise God for this answered prayer and for the gift of healing.  Continuing to keep you in my prayers, Susie! https://t.co/gEGLjWoRqJ

West Virginia is fueled by coal. I’m glad to see President Trump and the EPA are ending backwards regulations that would have extinguished the energy that powers our state and employs so many here in our communities. Thank you President Trump for advocating for our coal community!

https://t.co/GCBckGina7

I’m so happy that my staff had the opportunity to participate in Unite for Good’s meal-packing day in remembrance of the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks. It was a meaningful way to honor the lives lost and serve others in their memory. We will always remember. 🇺🇸 https://t.co/YFn2OUrQjM

Twenty-five years ago, our nation watched in horror as nearly 3,000 lives were taken in an attack on our country. We watched firefighters climb stairwells that others were fleeing, strangers carry strangers to safety, and a country that had been divided just hours before stand as one. 

A new generation is now coming of age who know September 11th only through the stories we tell them. That is why we must tell the stories of the lives lost, the heroes who ran toward danger knowing they may not make it out, and the unity that brought us together as one. We will never forget.

I am grateful to President Donald Trump and his Administration for delivering nearly $4.8 million to strengthen our rural healthcare workforce and expand preventive care across West Virginia! Read more about this new funding announcement below. ⬇️

https://t.co/szhheZTMBV

As we mark the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks this week, I want to take a moment to remember Dr. Paul Ambrose of Huntington, West Virginia.

A graduate of Marshall University, Dr. Ambrose went on to serve at the Office of the Surgeon General, dedicating his career to improving the health and well-being of others. On September 11, 2001, he was aboard Flight 77 when it was deliberately flown into the Pentagon.

May we never forget Dr. Ambrose and all the other innocent lives lost that day, as well as the countless families and communities forever changed by an act of pure evil.

The We Can’t Wait Act is a commonsense, bipartisan solution that gives Americans greater access to the benefits they have earned when they need them most. I will continue working to ensure Congress is doing everything possible to strengthen Social Security and make sure it works for the Americans who rely on it.

https://t.co/Sw837F9jZF

This evening, the Hershel “Woody” Williams National Medal of Honor Monument Location Act passed the House of Representatives, authorizing the construction of a monument in honor of Medal of Honor recipients on the National Mall. 

This bill was named in honor of the last surviving Medal of Honor recipient, and a fellow West Virginian, Hershel “Woody” Williams. Woody was awarded the Medal of Honor for his service in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserves during the Battle of Iwo Jima in World War II and spent the remainder of his life advocating fiercely for veterans and Gold Star families across the country. I can think of no one more deserving of this honor.

Today, on National Overdose Awareness Day, we remember the lives lost to overdose and stand with the families and communities who continue to feel its devastating impact.

West Virginia knows the challenges of addiction and substance abuse all too well. But we also know that recovery is possible, and that there are resources and people ready to help.

From expanding access to treatment and recovery services to supporting prevention and strengthening our communities, there are real solutions to this crisis. As we continue working in Washington to support West Virginians, I encourage anyone struggling with substance use, or anyone who knows someone who is, to reach out and take advantage of the resources available.

You are not alone, and help is available.

📞 1-800-662-HELP (4357)

The Rural Residency Planning and Development Program is vital to addressing physician shortages in our communities. This $750,000 grant will improve access to quality care in southern West Virginia, and help Make America Healthy Again.

https://t.co/gh8On9ldaB
